length: 6 weeks · 18 lessons (3 a week), 2 of them optional
description: Students build a working model of force as a push or a pull, apply Newton’s three laws to everyday motion, then use energy transfer and the law of the lever to explain simple machines and a trebuchet’s throw. Five experiments build toward an open, class-shared investigation of how trebuchet range and arm spin change with counterweight mass, assessed by an open-booklet Investigation Test in Lesson 18.
notes: Every lesson has its own slide deck and its own booklet section in four parts: A Reading · B Theory and examples · C Practice · D Above level. Lessons 15–18 run from the [Trebuchet Investigation booklet](trebuchet-investigation.html).
**Lessons 11 and 14 are optional** Year 8 extensions; skip both and the unit runs in 16 lessons.

**Above level:** Newton’s laws by name and the equations of motion are Levels 9–10 (VC2S10U17); conservation of energy as a law is Levels 9–10 (VC2S10U15). Lessons 4–8 and 12–13 use them as tools for the experiments, not as Year 7 standards.

achievement.text: Explain how balanced and unbalanced forces, including gravity, change an object’s motion, represented with force diagrams; calculate the mechanical advantage of simple machines; analyse energy transfers and transformations for efficiency.

Develop hypotheses and reasoned predictions; plan reproducible, safe and ethical investigations and select equipment that records data precisely; organise data in tables and graphs; analyse patterns, trends and anomalies; identify assumptions and sources of error; support conclusions with evidence and communicate findings for a purpose. *The trebuchet investigation and test carry almost this whole strand.*
Explain how new evidence can lead to changes in scientific knowledge (Lesson 12’s reading on Galileo).

descriptors.text: Balanced and unbalanced forces acting on objects, including gravitational force, represented with force diagrams; changes in motion relate to mass and force
Simple machines, including the lever, change the direction and size of forces
Energy exists in different forms, including gravitational and elastic; energy transfers and transformations, and their efficiency
Scientific knowledge, including models and theories, can change in light of new evidence
Science inquiry — questioning and predicting (I01); planning and conducting (I02–I03); processing, modelling and analysing (I04–I05); evaluating (I06–I07); communicating (I08)
Levels 9–10, above level — Newton’s laws of motion and the equations of motion
Levels 9–10, above level — conservation of energy in energy transfers and transformations

prepare: Lesson 1’s opening quiz checks primary-school ideas about push/pull forces before anything new is taught.
Every later deck opens with a five-question review: three on the lesson before, two from older lessons.
review: The opening review quiz in every deck; Part C checked in class each lesson; an exit question closing each lesson.
Task 12’s odd-result discussion and the booklet-completion check in Lesson 17, ahead of the test.
diff: Reading and comprehension come before any calculation; worked examples are revealed one step at a time.
Sentence starters, word banks and a worked first row in red on every write-in table.
Experiment 4 and the lever lessons use masses and arm lengths only (no newtons) until Lesson 9 introduces force units for MA.
extension: Part D of every lesson, several flagged above level (VC2S10U17, VC2S10U15).
Optional Year 8 Lessons 11 and 14; Section C of the Trebuchet Investigation Test.

Paper and marking key are staff-only and not on this site
